entry.evidence: While knowledge on how these hydrological changes will propagate to suspended sediment dynamics is still scarce

steps.action: States the aim: identify the areas and processes most relevant to suspended sediment and discharge dynamics across spatial and temporal scales.
steps.quote: we aim to pinpoint the areas and processes most relevant to sediment dynamics in combination with discharge dynamics on several spatial and temporal scales

steps.action: Designs the analysis around three nested gauges (Vent, Sölden, Tumpen; 100 to 800 km2), linked to snow cover, glacier, precipitation and land cover data.
steps.quote: [...] on three combined discharge and sediment gauges in a nested catchment setup

steps.action: Takes 15 min discharge and turbidity-based SSC series as delivered by the Hydrographic Service (Vent, Tumpen) and TiWAG (Sölden), restricted to 2006 to 2020.
steps.quote: At the gauges in Vent and Tumpen, we used the data as received by the Hydrographic Service of Tyrol.

steps.action: Operates an automatic sampler at Sölden in 2019 and 2020 (regular, threshold and event triggers; 99 samples, gravimetric SSC) to extend the turbidity calibration to high concentrations.
steps.quote: We took additional water samples in 2019 and 2020 using automatic samplers (MAXX P6 L Vacuum) in order to improve the data situation

steps.action: Tests whether the new and the TiWAG sample sets share one turbidity–SSC relation (ANCOVA; TiWAG points within the prediction interval of the new model).
steps.quote: This showed no significant differences between the two linear models.

steps.action: Fits one linear turbidity–SSC model to all 367 samples (R2 = 0.84) and applies it to the full Sölden turbidity series.
steps.quote: we conclude that there is good enough agreement to estimate one linear model using all 367 available samples

steps.action: Compares the scatter of the calibration with coefficients of determination reported in other studies.
steps.quote: does not appear to be unusually high compared to other studies reporting similar coefficients of determination

steps.action: Computes sediment discharge, water and suspended sediment yields, specific yields per catchment, and weekly percentages of annual yield.
steps.quote: From the discharge and SSC data, we calculated sediment discharge

steps.action: Describes spatial differences in mean annual specific discharge and sSSY, and their split by season: highest in Vent, summer-dominated, high interannual variability.
steps.quote: Specific suspended sediment yield ( s SSY) is markedly higher in the Vent catchment

steps.action: Correlates annual sQ and sSSY with glacier cover among the sub-catchments (R2 0.74 and 0.25).
steps.quote: show significant positive correlations (significance level α = 0.01 ) with increasing glacier cover among the respective catchments

steps.action: Checks the glacier link within the Vent catchment against annual glacier mass balances (and the full series from 1976 for sQ); finds no relation between annual WY and SSY.
steps.quote: both s Q and s SSY in Vent correlate positively with the cumulative annual mass balances of Vernagt- and Hintereisferner

steps.action: Describes weekly seasonality: sediment export is confined to a narrower window than discharge and peaks in the ice-melt period.
steps.quote: Suspended sediment seasonality is even more pronounced than discharge seasonality

steps.action: Establishes, year by year over 15 years, that the spring onset of sediment export is synchronous at the three gauges.
steps.quote: the first sharp increase in SSY was always simultaneous at the three gauges

steps.action: Asks what explains the simultaneous sediment onset and its delay behind the rise in water yield.
steps.quote: To explore the simultaneous onset of sediment export at all sites and the delay compared to the initial rises in water yield

steps.action: Sets weekly psed against the MODIS-derived snow-free fraction for 250 m elevation bands (Figure 8, p. 662): the onset matches snowmelt above 2500 m.
steps.quote: The initial rise in p sed (WOY) at all gauges coincides with the onset of snowmelt above 2500 m.

steps.action: Sets aside the bands below 2500 m as the trigger of the onset, because their snowmelt always preceded the sediment rise.
steps.quote: the onset of snowpack removal in the areas below 2500 m always preceded the initial rise in suspended sediment

steps.action: Checks the snow-cover link in the opposite season: the autumn decline in export coincides with the first snow build-up.
steps.quote: In autumn, sediment export declines as soon as the first snow cover starts to build up

steps.action: Characterizes land cover and recent deglaciation by elevation band from CORINE data and glacier inventories (Figure 9, p. 663).
steps.quote: Moreover, the first glacier areas can be found above 2500 m

steps.action: Identifies Qsed events visually (2011 to 2020), classifies Vent events as precipitation- or melt-driven, and estimates their shares of annual WY and SSY.
steps.quote: The events associated with precipitation transported on average 21 % (min. 7 %–max. 40 %) of the annual SSY

steps.action: Uses duration curves of the full 15 min record (Figure 10) to check that the event shares from 2011 to 2020 hold for the whole series since 2006.
steps.quote: these proportions seem to be representative for the whole time series since 2006

steps.action: Proposes that a mass movement caused the extreme August 2014 event; no field observation is available.
steps.quote: We hypothesize that this was associated with mass movements

steps.action: Documents an observed rainfall-triggered mass-wasting event (28 August 2020) and its sediment export at Vent.
steps.quote: an extreme precipitation event of about 100 mm within 3 d led to a mass-wasting event onto the Hintereisferner

steps.action: Compares the yield magnitudes with values for other Ötztal and Stubai catchments and with the Alpine compilation of Hinderer et al. (2013).
steps.quote: which generally correspond well to values reported for other catchments in the Ötztal and Stubai Alps

steps.action: Explains the non-significant sQ–mass balance correlation for 2006 to 2020 by the leverage of single years (2014), rather than revising the glacier link.
steps.quote: We attribute this to the leverage of individual years such as 2014

steps.action: Sets the sSSY–glacier relation against the published understanding of glaciers as sediment sources (paraglacial, subglacial and proglacial supply).
steps.quote: is in line with the current understanding that glaciers act as important sediment sources

steps.action: Checks the MODIS snowmelt timing against independently reported snowmelt timing.
steps.quote: is well in accordance with the timing as reported by Kuhn et al. (2016)

steps.action: Concludes that areas above 2500 m are the crucial source areas and that sediment supply is limited while they are snow-covered or frozen.
steps.quote: we conclude that the areas above 2500 m are crucial source areas, where the determining processes are activated as the snow melts

steps.action: Compares the event shares of annual SSY with other glaciated catchments and with fluvial systems.
steps.quote: Similar proportions have been reported for other glaciated catchments (Leggat et al., 2015; Wulf et al., 2012)

steps.action: Keeps the claim that thermally induced export currently yields the largest share of SSY, while single rainstorms involving mass movements can carry up to 26 %.
steps.quote: thermally induced sediment export through snow and glacier melt yields the biggest share of SSY in Vent

steps.action: Draws on published climate and cryosphere projections to suggest that precipitation-driven mass-movement events will gain importance.
steps.quote: heavy precipitation events have the potential to drastically gain in importance with regard to sediment export

tree.answer: Suspended sediment and discharge dynamics in glaciated nested catchments; synchronous spring sediment onset found
Partly: SSC is inferred from turbidity through calibration, and yields are computed
Identify crucial source areas, time periods and processes
Informal rivals: elevation bands below vs above 2500 m; thermal vs precipitation-driven export
Different onset timing relative to band-wise snowmelt; different event shares of SSY
Conditions found: gauged years and catchments, one observed mass-wasting event

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Yes: 15 years, three nested gauges, spring and autumn transitions
Partly: holds across individual years and in autumn; the sQ–mass balance link fails for 2006 to 2020
Areas above 2500 m are crucial; thermal export dominates; best explanation

end.claim: Areas above 2500 m a.s.l. (glacier tongues, bare rock, recently deglaciated zones) are the crucial suspended-sediment source areas: their snowmelt gates the synchronous spring onset of export, and thermally induced export currently dominates over precipitation events.

decisive_move.sentence: Setting weekly sediment-yield percentages against MODIS snow-free fractions by 250 m elevation band shows that the synchronous onset coincides with snowmelt above 2500 m; without this synopsis the source-area claim would not exist.

gates.evidence: Most data were existing monitoring series. The new sampling served calibration, not a hypothesis (§2.2.1 ¶4). The coincidence test could have failed: the onset could have tracked snowmelt below 2500 m, and the paper reports that it did not (§3.4 ¶3). No formal test against stated rivals was run. Event detection was visual, by expert judgement (§2.2.2 ¶2). Nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: ANCOVA and Shapiro–Wilk tests to justify pooling calibration samples

novelty_claims.quote: To our knowledge, this study represents the first extensive analysis of discharge and suspended sediment dynamics on multiple spatial and temporal scales
which to date few studies have done
However, as an advantage over the ACDA, which yields the percentage of unfrozen area for the whole catchment, we are able to differentiate

limits: No peer-review file or discussion was supplied, although the paper names two referees and an editor, so no review sequence is coded. Rivals are not stated before the results. The 'X' at step 16 is the coder's inference from a descriptive sentence, and the processes above 2500 m (subglacial, proglacial, permafrost, hillslope) are not separated (§3.4 ¶3, §4.4 ¶2). The calibration uncertainty (R2 = 0.84) is not propagated into the yields. The Vent and Tumpen calibrations are used as received, and 2019 to 2020 data were not quality-checked (§2.2.1 ¶3). Winter SSC at Vent and Sölden is missing and set to zero (Table 3). Event identification is visual and not reproducible from the text. The Shapiro–Wilk p = 0.03 is called 'normal'; at alpha = 0.05 this would indicate non-normality (coder observation, not discussed by the authors). The headline claim's composition sits between natures_repetition and trace_series, because the claim is explanatory but rests on conditions repeated by nature. Sub-claims and their statuses: the sQ and sSSY correlation with glacier cover across five (sub-)catchments is regularity_in_range (sSSY R2 = 0.25); the within-Vent sSSY–mass balance correlation is regularity_in_range (alpha = 0.05), while the sQ link fails for 2006 to 2020 and is explained post hoc; the event shares of SSY (25 %, 26 %, 21 %) are estimate_with_resolution, with min–max ranges only; the turbidity–SSC calibration is capability_characterized; the 2014 mass-movement hypothesis is untested (none); the future increase in events is cited expectation only.

disagreements.target: Prior studies comparing mean annual yields across sites, or resolving dynamics at only one or two locations
disagreements.support: The nested three-gauge, high-resolution design is offered as the missing combination of spatial and temporal resolution.
disagreements.quote: However, it is crucial to consider discharge and sediment dynamics in high temporal resolution as well as their spatial patterns

disagreements.target: Active contributing drainage area (ACDA), Li et al. (2021)
disagreements.support: Band-wise snow-free fractions resolve areas within the catchment, where the ACDA gives a single catchment-wide percentage.
disagreements.quote: However, as an advantage over the ACDA, which yields the percentage of unfrozen area for the whole catchment, we are able to differentiate

disagreements.target: Areal precipitation estimates for the Vent catchment (Hanzer et al., 2018; Kuhn et al., 2016; Stoll et al., 2020)
disagreements.support: Observed specific discharge nearly equals estimated precipitation; the authors explain this by non-equilibrium glacier melt.
disagreements.quote: [...] compared to areal precipitation estimates for the Vent catchment between 1200 and 1500

disagreements.target: Glacier cover–yield correlations across spatially distinct Alpine catchments (Hinderer et al., 2013; Lalk et al., 2014; Schöber and Hofer, 2018)
disagreements.support: The same positive correlation is found within a nested setup, which the authors contrast with the distinct-catchment designs.
disagreements.quote: [...] correlations have been reported across the European Alps for spatially distinct catchments

disagreements.target: Event-dominated sediment transport in fluvial systems (Delaney et al., 2018b)
disagreements.support: Events carry about 25 % of SSY here, against up to 90 % in fluvial systems; the authors read this as greater sediment availability in glaciated catchments.
disagreements.quote: compared to fluvial systems wherein up to 90 % of sediment is transported during short, high-discharge events

alternatives_considered.chosen: Visual, expert-based identification of Qsed events
alternatives_considered.reason: Thresholds are unsuitable due to intense interannual and seasonal variability in Qsed

alternatives_considered.chosen: Low precipitation threshold (>3 mm in 24 h) for classifying precipitation events
alternatives_considered.reason: Point measurements underestimate catchment precipitation because of spatial variability and topography

alternatives_considered.chosen: Event analysis at Vent and Tumpen only, 2011–2020; precipitation classification at Vent only

alternatives_considered.chosen: Weekly averaging, without differentiating the bands above 2500 m
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Finer temporal or band-wise analysis above 2500 m
